title: Water movement in the unsaturated zone at a low-level radioactive-waste burial site near Barnwell, South Carolina
citation: Dennehy, K.F., and McMahon, P.B., 1989, Water movement in the unsaturated zone at a low-level radioactive-waste burial site near Barnwell, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Water-Supply Paper 2345, map scale 1:345,000.
notes:
Hydrology report on the unsaturated zone; geology is brief (page 10). Monitoring sites recorded as 'other' observations with ground elevations from Table 1 (page 14). Instrument positions, tensions, saturations, tracer rates and conductance curves (pages 14-34) are not recorded; the compacted clayey-sand cap/barrier is engineered fill and its properties are skipped. Figure pages 15-19, 21-23, 25-34 are graphs with garbled text. Ksat table on page 21 has a garbled text layer; units header reads 'Ksat(C/n/S)' (cm/s). Packet 2 continues the report.
Continues packet 1. Tritium concentrations (Table 3, page 37), tracer velocities, model grid details and error analysis are not recorded (not geologic units or aquifer properties). Graph pages 36, 38, 40, 42-44 have garbled labels. References: kept South Carolina site and regional entries; skipped general methods and national references (ASTM, Bowen, Brooks and Corey, Brutsaert, Campbell, Davis and Neuman, Drever, EPA, Freeze and Cherry, Freeze and Witherspoon, Hung, Neff, Purcell, state health department 1984 monitoring report, Thatcher and others, NOAA, Winter).
Re-read of pages 24 and 37. Table 2 (p. 24): porosity, residual saturation, lambda and saturated hydraulic conductivity per sample, one water test per value; porosity, residual saturation and lambda have no printed units. Three Ksat values whose exponent the text layer garbles (xlO) were read from the page image. Site 3 tensiometer depths are from the text on p. 24 and flagged inferred as sample depths. Percent-saturation statements in the p. 24 text (site 2, January and May 1983) were not recorded as tests. Table 3 (p. 37): tritium in soil moisture; the text layer garbles the ± sign throughout, so every concentration was read from the page image; site 1 cells give two results (footnote 1 lab / footnote 2 lab) recorded separately; "-" cells skipped; three site 2 dates read 11/50/84 in the text and 11/30/84 in the image.
